objects.who: door|Barred from inside, with two planks and a spite.^Nobody has lived here since before the sleep. Somebody keeps the roof very tidy, and there is a ladder up to it.
objects.say: The bar comes off. The door of the goat's house stands open.^The goat does not use it. The goat has never needed a door.

objects.text: Bolted. The sisters who weave here have not spoken to each other in nine years, or to the street in ten.^There is a ladder at the east end. The cats use it.

objects.who: door|The door of the counting house. There is more bronze on it than on a shield.^It opens to the gong, for people who have come to pay. Nobody has rung it in forty nights. Nobody rang it much before.
objects.say: The gong sings, and somewhere inside a bolt remembers its duty.^The counting house is open for business. It is the only thing in Ashkel that is.

objects.text: The fishing boats, all in, tied up tight.^Forty nights, and nobody has asked the fish how they feel about it.
Nets, folded for a morning that hasn't come yet.^The road ends here. So does the land.
